subject: zoology
question_text: Distinguish between lotic and lentic habitats.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.61, VSAQ 158). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Lentic habitats
lines: Lentic habitats are the STILL water bodies.
The water in them does not flow from place
steps.why: The pair is marked as a contrast, so each side needs the same two things — whether the water moves, and a named example — and writing them in the same order makes the contrast visible to the examiner.
common_mistakes: Giving a river as a lentic habitat. A river flows, so it is lotic.
Writing only the examples with no statement about the water.
steps.memory_tip: Lentic and level both start the same way: level water is still water.
steps.margin_note: One line on the water, one line of examples. Keep both sides in the same order.

steps.label: Lotic habitats

lines.text: Lentic = still water, Lotic = flowing water

lines: Lotic habitats are the FLOWING water bodies.
The water in them moves in one direction.
steps.why: Naming the direction of the water is the whole distinction, so the second half repeats the first half's shape with the one word changed from still to flowing.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two terms. Lotic is the flowing one.
Giving a reservoir as lotic. A reservoir holds still water, so it is lentic.
steps.memory_tip: LOtic = flOwing. The other one, lentic, is the still one.
steps.margin_note: Answer as a two-line contrast. The box gives the examiner the difference at a glance.

insider_note: A one-word slip loses both marks here, so fix the flowing one first: lotic is the moving water.
